SCOPE (verifier): items 8.4.2, 8.4.3, 8.6.3, 8.7.1 and 8.7.4 are covered only by compact primitive-graph prediction worlds (plan_spoilage, plan_serial_stages, dl_delayed_adoption, net_congestion_routes, net_interdependent); in them the participant runs experiments and predicts, it never allocates, routes or targets. Their decision worlds (plan_perishable, des_perishable, plan_supply_chain, net_routing, net_cascade, pe_rollout_targeting) remain dominated: on several seeds even the private oracle is within 0.8 of the best simple policy (static-tuning worlds), and the public references are well below the oracle.

Prediction families (24 of the 62 admitted training families) are scored 1 - MSE / variance of the truth at held-out conditions; their scripted references assume the model class of the mechanism (D-64), so a reference score of 0.9-1.0 shows feasibility, not that a generic learner can do it; the hold-and-fit predictors show that a generic curve fitter cannot.
Realised revenue in prediction worlds is a Gaussian relative scatter (0.1 x observation_noise) around the expected rate; realised sales do not feed back into stocks.

Compute in program worlds is billed per call in quanta (100 units, plus 10,000 per whole 10,000 measured): a call of up to about 3.5 ms of CPU costs the same as an empty one; a call near a quantum boundary could still be billed differently under load (the references stay below a fifth of a quantum).

The 8.10 check of prediction families freezes timed regimes and exogenous stocks at the end of the first fifth; a change carried by a lever-driven stock (path dependence inside a held condition, as in mk_drift) is not counted as a change of the world.

Seventeen families became prediction tasks (D-63 and its amendment): their objective is the interventional or end-of-episode response at held-out settings, scored 1 - MSE / variance of the truth; their public references are model-fitting procedures (refs_adapt), several of them assuming a model class (a logit demand curve, a drifting bump, a rival that follows your average price, a peaked dose law, a saturating hub, a saturating output link).

Several prediction references are weak on one seed of a seed set (ch_sign_reversal, ch_demand_shift, cxc_balancing_constraint, cxc_latched_reversal); they pass the two-of-three rule, the margin is small.
Program-execution families pay compute by measured CPU time (D-20 metering); admission values of pe_* families can vary with machine load.
The planning families of 8.4.1-8.4.3 and the routing/cascade network families (8.7.1, 8.7.4) remain static-tuning or weak-reference worlds; their redesigns were reverted.
